title: The Divergence Theorem and a Unified Theory
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar

definitions.title: The Divergence Theorem (Gauss's Theorem)
definitions.statement: The net outward flux of a continuously differentiable vector field F across a closed orientable surface S enclosing solid region D equals the triple integral of the divergence of F over D.
conditions: S is a piecewise-smooth closed surface
n is outward pointing unit normal
definitions.explanation: Internal sources and sinks expand outward, so total surface flux equals the volume integral of local volumetric expansion rates.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Transforms two-dimensional closed surface flux integrals into three-dimensional volume integrals.

definitions.title: Divergence as Volumetric Source Density
definitions.statement: The divergence div F at point P is the limiting outward flux per unit volume as the volume shrinks to P. If div F > 0, P is a source; if div F < 0, P is a sink; if div F = 0 everywhere, F is incompressible (solenoidal).
conditions: Volume shrinks smoothly to point P
definitions.explanation: Physical foundation for continuity equations in hydrodynamics and Gauss's law in electrodynamics.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Divergence quantifies the local rate of fluid generation per unit volume.
